name: Pomerol

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: Pomerol is a Right Bank appellation in the Libournais, and its wine is predominately Merlot with Cabernet Franc in a supporting role.
There is no official classification of Pomerol wine, though Château Pétrus is widely held to be equivalent to premier cru.
The sub-soil is dark packed clay with a high iron content, and the plateau stands on a gravel bank.
Pomerol is the smallest of the major fine wine regions in Bordeaux, and almost all the wine is estate-bottled.
The AOC rules from 1936 outlawed plantings of any white grape varieties.
The wine will typically receive 18 to 20 months of aging in barriques prior to bottling and release.

blurb.text: A Right Bank commune in Bordeaux whose wine is mostly Merlot with Cabernet Franc in support. It has no real village, just a church among the vines, and became AOC in 1936.
